about: Twelve laws on marriages in trouble. A wife who plays the fool, wastes her house and belittles her husband is convicted; if he divorces her she gets nothing for her journey or her divorce payment, and if he does not, he may take a second woman while she stays on in his house as a servant (§141). A woman who rejects her husband has her case examined: if she is blameless she takes her dowry and goes home, and if not she is thrown into the water (§142–143). Then the slave-woman and the šugītum, two women beside the wife: a husband whose wife gave him a slave-woman who bore sons may not take a šugītum (§144); a husband whose wife bore him no sons may (§145), but the šugītum does not rank with the wife; a slave-woman who bears sons and then rivals her mistress cannot be sold, though the mistress may mark her as a slave, and if she bore none the mistress may sell her (§146–147). A husband whose wife falls ill may take another woman but may not divorce the sick one (§148); if she will not stay, she leaves with her dowry (§149). A wife given property by deed passes it to the son she loves (§150). Last, debts: a husband’s earlier debts cannot be collected from his wife, nor a wife’s earlier debts from her husband, but a debt made during the marriage is paid by both (§151–152). Harper’s transliteration writes the Sumerian signs for ‘woman’, ‘house’, ‘silver’, ‘merchant’ and ‘slave-woman’ as Akkadian words, and each of them was read from the plate; the few doubtful spellings are marked in the notes.

sentences.i: If a man’s wife, who is living in a man’s house, has set her face to go out, and plays the fool,
sentences.n: A new law, and it opens with a long “if”: read it as a chain of clauses. šumma begins it, aššat awīlim is “the wife of a man” (aššat is aššatum in the construct state, “wife of”, with awīlim in the genitive), and ša ina bīt awīlim wašbat is a relative clause, “who is living in a man’s house” (wašbat, “she dwells”, is the stative of wašābum, as in §130). ana wuṣîm is ana + infinitive, “to go out”: the first sign is PI, which reads wa or wu, and the infinitive of waṣûm is wuṣûm. panīša ištakan, “she has set her face”, is the idiom for making up one’s mind (iškun “he set” in the perfect, with -ta- after the first sign: ištakan); -ma ties it to the next clause. zikiltam izakkil sets a noun beside a verb of the same root, “she plays the fool’s part”: Harper’s glossary files the two words under šikiltu “the part of a fool” and šakālu “to play the part of a fool” (his text spells them with z, and the lemmas here follow the signs); that is his sense, and the pair is UNCERTAIN by later standards. The wife’s misconduct goes on into the next unit.

sentences.n: More of her conduct, then the verdict begins. bīssa is bītum “house” + -ša “her”: the t and the š meet and are said ss, and the plate writes the house-sign É followed by the sign ZA (Harper’s bî-za). uzappaḫ is the D-stem of sapāḫum “to scatter”, here “to neglect” (Harper: “to scatter, to neglect”), present tense. mussa is mutum “husband” + -ša “her”, written mu-za (the spelling used throughout §127–140), and ušamṭa is the Š-stem of maṭûm “to be small”, “to make small, belittle” (Harper: “to make little, to belittle”), present tense like uzappaḫ: the present of a Š-stem of a verb ending in a vowel ends in -â, the preterite in -i, and the signs spell -a. Harper prints the sign DA as da; the verb needs it read ṭa. The exact vowel is UNCERTAIN. ukannūšima is the D-stem of kânum “to be firm” — “to prove against, convict” — with -ši “her” and -ma “and”: this is the start of the apodosis, and the sentence goes on.

sentences.i: If her husband has said, “I divorce her,” he shall divorce her; nothing shall be given to her for her journey (?) or her divorce payment.
sentences.n: A divorce by the husband’s word, with the word quoted. ezibša is what he says: ezēbum “to leave, to divorce” + -ša “her”. Harper prints e-ṣi-ib-ša; the sign is ZI and is read zi here, as in izzibši and īzibšim. The form itself is UNCERTAIN: the object “her” on a verb is normally -ši, so -ša is unexpected; the quoted sense “I divorce her” is fixed by the clause that follows. iqtabi is the perfect of qabûm “to say” and closes the quotation; the code’s “says” is a perfect, “has said”. izzibši, “he shall divorce her”, is the present of ezēbum with -ši “her”. ḫarrānša and uzubbûša are two payments she does not get: uzubbûm is “divorce payment” (a rare word, Harper’s reading), and ḫarrānum is Harper’s “way, road, journey, errand”, so ḫarrānša “her journey” is a guess at a travel-allowance (UNCERTAIN); Harper’s own translation takes it as “on her departure”. mimma ul innaddiššim is “nothing shall be given to her”: innaddin is the N-stem (passive) of nadānum “to give”, and the n of the stem is swallowed before -šim “to her” (the signs iš-ši-im).

The opening is as §144: šumma awīlum aššatam iḫuzma. mārī lā ušaršīšuma is Harper’s u-šar-ši-šu-ma: rašûm “to get, acquire” in the Š-stem is “to cause (someone) to acquire”, with two objects: ušarši + -šu “him” + -ma, “she has not made him acquire sons” (the same verb is in §137: ušaršušu). The exact vowels of the ending are UNCERTAIN. The rest of the “if” repeats §144.

sentences.i: If she has not borne sons, her mistress may sell her for silver.
sentences.n: §147, the other case in a single clause. lā ūlid is “she did not bear” (ūlid, the preterite). Then the words of the last law without ul: bēlissa ana kaspim inaddišši, “her mistress shall give her for silver”, that is, she may sell her; the plain present is again a permission, and the contrast with ul inaddišši in §146 is the whole law.

sentences.i: If a man has taken a wife and a sickness (laʾbum) has seized her,
sentences.n: §148, the sick wife. aššatam iḫuzma as before; Harper prints šuma for šumma on the plate line, which is a misprint (the signs are šum-ma). laʾbum is Harper’s la-ʾa-bu-um, which he glosses “fever, disease”: what the illness is, is UNCERTAIN, and the translation says “a sickness”. iṣṣabassi is the perfect of ṣabātum “to seize” + -ši “her”: the t of the perfect and the š of -ši meet and are said ss, “it has seized her” (the same verb is in §151).

to answer; to satisfy, pay (a creditor): ippalma (present, with -ma) “he shall pay, and”

sentences.i: both of them shall pay the merchant.
sentences.n: kilallašunu is Harper’s ki-la-la-šu-nu: kilallān “both” + -šunu “of them”, “both of them”. tamkāram is “the merchant”, the creditor, accusative: DAM.GÀR, the two Sumerian signs (Harper prints it as a single word without hyphens; the plate row is longer than the signs of tamkāram and ippalū alone, so a complement is possible, UNCERTAIN). ippalū is the present plural of apālum “to pay” (Harper’s i-ip-pa-lu): “they shall pay”. The debt is theirs together, and the creditor can be paid by both. This is the last law of the part; §153 follows.

glossary.-anni: me (1st-person singular accusative suffix, on a verb; the ventive -am + -ni): taḫḫazanni (ta-aḫ-ḫa-za-an-ni) “you take me”
glossary.-ma: and (clause-chaining particle); also “it is X that…”
glossary.-ša: her / its (3rd-person feminine suffix) · on nouns, “her”: after a t the š is assimilated and said ss, spelled with the sign ZA: bīssa (bi-za, or É-za) “her house”, mussa (mu-za) “her husband”, warkassa (wa-ar-ka-za) “her case”, bēlissa (be-li-za) “her mistress”; otherwise written plainly: panīša, mutiša, abiša, šeriqtaša, bēltiša · on an infinitive, the object “her”: ṣabātiša “seizing her” · on a verb-like form: ezibša (e-zi-ib-ša, UNCERTAIN in form) · on a plural noun: mārūša (DUMU{meš}-ša) “her sons”
glossary.-ši: her / it (3rd-person feminine singular suffix, on a verb): ukannūšima “they shall convict her”, inaddûši “they shall throw her”, iqallûši “they shall burn her” · iṣṣabassi (iṣ-ṣa-ba-az-zi) “it has seized her” (the t of the perfect + -ši said ss, spelled -zi) · on the present plural: imannûši “they shall count her”, ibaqqarūši “they shall claim against her” · on the Š-stem: ušērribši “he shall bring her in”, ušamṭaši “he has belittled her”
glossary.-šim: to her, for her (dative suffix -šim, on a verb; the feminine counterpart of -šum): inaddiššim “he shall give her”, utarrūšim “they shall return to her”, inaddinūšimma “they shall give her, and”, ušallamšimma “he shall make (it) whole for her, and”; not the accusative -ši “her” of ukabbilšima and ubbiršima
glossary.-šu: his / him · -šum “to him, for him” (dative): išakkanūšum, innadnušum · after a dental the suffix is assimilated and spelled with z: …ssu (ṣibat-zu, ṣibassu “its interest”, written after a broken sign); with a noun: ṣibtišu “its interest”, qātīšu “his hand”, damqaršu “his merchant”; tu-šu, te-šu in broken forms · with the same assimilation after a t: aššassu (aš-ša-zu) “his wife”, from aššat + -šu, t + š said ss · on a verb, the object “him”, or “to him” in the dative (Harper writes -šu for -šum): imaggarūšu (i-ma-ag-ga-ru-šu) “they shall agree to him”; on a noun after a preposition: elišu “upon him”
glossary.abbuttum: UNCERTAIN: Harper “service, slavery”; later dictionaries read a mark of slavery: abbuttam (ab-bu-ut-tam, accusative), used with šakānum “to set, impose” (abbuttam išakkan); the sense is not secure
glossary.adi: up to, times: adi 12-šu “twelvefold” · as a conjunction, “as long as”, with the subjunctive: adi kirâm ṣabtu “as long as he holds the orchard” · adu 3-šu, adu 6-šu “three times, six times (as much)” — the multiplier, spelled a-du (Harper’s variant of adi; the plate has the sign DU)
glossary.alākum: to go: illak “he shall go” · illiku “(where) he went” (preterite, subjunctive -u, after a restored ašar), in the agent law · alākišu (a-la-ki-šu) “his going” (infinitive with -šu): ina alākišu “in his going” · Gt present ittallak (it-ta-al-la-ak) “she shall go away” (the Gt gives the sense of going off; the Gtn would be ittanallak)
glossary.amtum: slave-woman (GEME₂) · amassu (GEME₂-zu) “his slave-woman”, amtam (GEME₂-am), amtim (GEME₂-tim) · plural amâti (GEME₂{meš}) “slave-women”; the exact plural signs are UNCERTAIN
glossary.ana: to, for · with an infinitive, “to, for” (ana kirîm zaqāpim “to plant as an orchard”); “as” (ana kirîm), “into” (ana libbi), “at the rate of” (ana itêšu)
glossary.apālum: to answer; to satisfy, pay (a creditor): ippalma (present, with -ma) “he shall pay, and”
glossary.awīlum: man; the free citizen, the code’s first legal class
glossary.aššatum: wife: ana aššatišu “to his wife” · aššassu (SAL-zu, ZU for -ssu) “his wife” · construct aššat (aš-ša-at) “wife of” before a genitive: aššat awīlim · aššatam, aššatim, aššatum, written SAL (the same sign as zinništum “woman”) or aš-ša-tam
glossary.aššum: because (of); concerning · because; with a clause, also “so that”, giving purpose or reason (aššum … lā ṣabātiša, UNCERTAIN in grammar)
glossary.aḫûm: outside, other: ilkum aḫûm “another (kind of) tenure”
glossary.aḫāzum: to take, grasp; Š-stem šūḫuzum “to make take hold” · to take (a wife): iḫuz (i-ḫu-uz) preterite, iḫuzma “he took, and”; present iḫḫaz (i-iḫ-ḫa-az) “he shall take”, which also serves as a permission, “he may take”; iḫḫazu (i-iḫ-ḫa-zu, with the subjunctive -u) “(before) he takes”; infinitive aḫāzim (a-ḫa-zi-im), taking its object in the genitive; taḫḫazanni (2nd person, with -anni “me”)
glossary.babtum: UNCERTAIN: Harper’s “loss, defects”, but in §126 apparently the party accused of the loss, “the one blamed” (later dictionaries have babtum as a city quarter or ward, which would be a group held liable): babtašu, babtišu (ba-ab-ta-šu, ba-ab-ti-šu) “his babtum”; the sense is not secure
glossary.balāṭum: to live; D-stem bulluṭum — muballiṭ “who gives life” · stative baltat (ba-al-ṭa-at) “she lives”, in adi baltat “as long as she lives”
glossary.baqārum: to claim, make a claim against (Harper: BAKARU “to make claim”): ibaqqarūši (i-ba-qa₂-ru-ši, present plural, “they shall claim against her”) with -ši “her”; Harper prints the sign as ga, read qa₂
glossary.bašûm: to exist, arise: ibbaššû “which arose” · lā ibaššišum “there is not to him” (= he has none), with dative -šum · in broken forms …ši (ul ibašši, “there is not”, the verb itself restored); ibaššû “which are (there)”, in mimma ina qātīšu ibaššû · ibašši (i-ba-aš-ši, present) “there is, is upon”: ḫubullum elišu ibašši “a debt is upon him”
glossary.bašûm-N: N-stem of bašûm: to be there, be found: ibbaššû (present, 3rd plural, in a ša-clause) “which are found” · ittabši (it-tab-ši, perfect) “it has come about, has happened”
glossary.bašûm-Š: Š-stem of bašûm “to exist”: to bring into being, produce (a crop): uštabši “he has produced” (perfect)
glossary.bēltum: lady, mistress (the feminine of bēlum): bēltiša (be-el-ti-ša) “her mistress”; bēlissa (be-li-za) “her mistress”, from the construct bēlit + -ša, t + š said ss
glossary.bēlum: owner, lord: bēl ḫulqim “owner of the lost property” · owner of a field, bēl eqlim; bēl ḫubullim “creditor” · bēl kirîm “owner of the orchard” · bēl (be-el), the construct “owner of”, also with a suffix on the noun that follows: bēl ḫubullišu “his creditor”, bēl ḫubulliša “her creditor”
glossary.bītum: house, estate · bīt karānim “wine-house, tavern” (construct form bīt, written É); bītiša “her house” (É-ša) · bīt awīlim “a man’s house”; bīssa (bi-za, É-za) “her house”, written with É or syllabically with BI + ZA; bītišu (É-šu) “his house”; genitive bītim, accusative bītam, written É alone
glossary.bīšum: movable property, goods, possessions: bīšašu “his goods” · short construct form bīš (bi-iš) before a genitive: bīš qātīšu “his own goods”
glossary.eli: against, upon · with suffixes: elišu, eliša, elišunu “upon him, her, them” (of a debt)
glossary.epēšum: to do, make: epēšim “doing” · to work (land): ippeš(ma) (present): eqlam šipram ippeš “he shall do the work on the field” · to build (?) (a house): bītam ippēšma(?) “he builds a house, and”, the verb broken; iteppuš (?) in a broken line · ippešū (i-ib-bi-šu) “they shall do (work), they shall work” (present plural) · īpušu (i-pu-šu, preterite with the subjunctive -u) “(which) he built”: to make, build (a house)
glossary.eqlum: field (written A.ŠÀ): eqelšu “his field” — the fief-land this whole block protects · bound form eqel (eqel itêšu “his neighbour’s field”; eqel ušākilu “the field he grazed”)
glossary.erēbum: to enter: iterub “she has entered” (perfect; Harper I,2) · irrubu (i-ir-ru-bu) “she enters” and īrubu (i-ru-bu) “she entered” — present and preterite with the subjunctive -u, after lāma “before” and ištu “after”
glossary.erēbum-Š: Š-stem of erēbum “to enter”: to make enter, bring in: ušērribši (u-še-ir-ri-ib-ši) “he shall bring her in”, with -ši “her”
glossary.ezēbum: to leave; Š-stem šūzubum: ušēzib “he deposited (a document)” · īzib (preterite) “he left (over)” · to leave, divorce: izzibši (i-iz-zi-ib-ši, present, “he shall divorce her”) · ezibša (e-zi-ib-ša) “(I) divorce her”, a quoted word, UNCERTAIN in form (the object “her” on a verb is normally -ši) · īzibšim (i-zi-ib-ši-im, preterite) “he left to her”, said of a deed or gift left to someone
glossary.ezēbum-Š: UNCERTAIN: Š-stem of ezēbum “to leave”: to have left, have deposited (a document): uštēzib (uš-te-zi-ib, perfect, 3rd person); the Š-stem šūzubum elsewhere means “to save, rescue”, so the sense with a tablet (ṭuppam uštēzib) rests on the context
glossary.ina: in, from · at (ina ebūrim “at harvest”); out of (ina bilat kirîm “out of the orchard’s yield”) · “through, by (means of)”: ina maḫāṣim “through beating”, ina pilšim “by a breach”; “regarding”: ina mimma ša … “regarding whatever …”; ina šanat “in the year”
glossary.itti: with · “from”, after leqûm “to take”: itti šarrāqānišu ileqqi “from his thief he shall take”
glossary.ištu: after, since; from; as a conjunction, “after, once”: ištu … īteliānim “after … have come up”
glossary.išûm: to have: lā īšu “he has not” · īšu “he has”, īšû (the subjunctive form, in a clause that continues): ana turrim lā īšû “has not to repay”
glossary.kaspum: silver — the code’s money, written KÙ.BABBAR “shining precious-metal” · kaspim: mišil mana kaspim “half a mina of silver” · with a spelled vowel after the logogram: KÙ.BABBAR-a-am, -i-im, -u-um: kaspam, kaspim, kaspum (accusative, genitive, nominative); kaspum as the subject; the grain-and-silver pair šeʾam u kaspam “grain and silver”
glossary.kilallān: both (of two): kilallašunu (ki-la-la-šu-nu) “both of them”, with -šunu “their, of them”
glossary.kirûm: orchard, garden (written {giš}SAR, the KIRI₆ sign): kirāšu “his orchard”
glossary.kânum-D: D-stem of kânum: to convict, prove against someone (uktīn, ukannūšuma) · uktīn (uk-ti-in, perfect, with the infixed -t-) “he has convicted”; ukannūšuma (u-ka-an-nu-šu-ma, present, plural, with -šu “him” and -ma) “they shall convict him, and”; ukānma (u-ka-an-ma, present, singular) “he shall convict, and”
glossary.kīma: like, as · as, like; with a verb in the subjunctive: kīma ubbalu “as he brings (it)” · according to: kīma ṣimdat šarrim “according to the king’s schedule” · “since, when”, before a stative: kīma mimmûšu lā ḫalqu “since his goods are not lost”
glossary.laʾbum: UNCERTAIN: a sickness, disease (Harper “fever, disease”): laʾbum (la-a-bu-um, nominative); what illness is meant is not known
glossary.leqûm: to take: ileqqi “he shall take” · ilqi “he took” (il-qi₂), ilqû (subjunctive, il-qu₂-u₂), ilqēma (il-qi₂-e-ma) “he took, and”, ilteqēma (perfect, il-te-qi₂-ma) “he has taken, and”; ša … ilqû “which he took” · ilqēma (il-qi₂-ma) “he took, and” (preterite ilqe + -ma, here without a spelled e); ilteqe (il-te-qi₂, perfect) “he has taken”; ileqqi (i-li-qi₂, present) “he shall take”; leqîm (li-qi₂-im, infinitive, genitive): ina kaspim leqîm “in the taking of the silver”
glossary.lā: not (in subordinate and nominal contexts) · before a noun in the genitive, “without”: lā kanīkim “without a sealed receipt”; in a šumma-clause, “not”: lā ītamar “he did not see”
glossary.lāma: before (la-ma), as a conjunction with a verb in the subjunctive: lāma … iḫḫazu “before he takes”
glossary.magārum: to agree, consent: imtagarma (perfect, with -ma) “has come to an agreement”, said of a settlement made with another party (itti …) · imaggarūšu (i-ma-ag-ga-ru-šu, present plural + -šu) “they shall agree to him” · imtagar (im-ta-gar, perfect) “she has agreed” (ana + infinitive)
glossary.manûm-count: to count, reckon (the verb; the noun manûm “mina” is another word): imannû(ma) “they shall count” — 3rd plural, impersonal
glossary.maḫārum-Št: UNCERTAIN: Št-stem of maḫārum “to face, be level with”, reflexive: to make oneself equal to (Harper: III,2, “to take precedence of”): uštamaḫḫar (uš-ta-ma-aḫ-ḫa-ar, present) and uštatamḫir (uš-ta-tam-ḫi-ir, perfect, with the t of the perfect after the stem’s š); the exact nuance is not secure
glossary.maṭûm-Š: Š-stem of maṭûm “to be small”: to make small, belittle (Harper: “to make little, to belittle”): ušamṭa (u-ša-am-ṭa, present, 3rd person, read as ušamṭâ: the present of a Š-stem of a verb ending in a vowel ends in -â, the preterite in -i), ušamṭaši (u-ša-am-ṭa-ši) “he belittles her”, with -ši “her”; Harper prints the sign as da, read ṭa; the exact vowel is UNCERTAIN
glossary.mutum: husband (short u; Harper “husband”; mūtum “death” is another word, spelled the same, so the sense rests on context): mutiša “her husband”, mussa “her husband” (written mu-za, -ša after the t), mut “husband of” (construct; mut libbiša “the husband of her heart”)
glossary.mārum: son (DUMU) — here: a minor, not yet able to sell · member of a group: mārū ugārim (DUMU A.GÀR{meš}) “the sons of the irrigated land”, the district’s farmers · mār awīlim “a man’s son” (DUMU); mārī (DUMU{meš}) “sons” (oblique plural, which may include daughters, so “children”); māršu (DUMU-šu) “his son” · mārūša (DUMU{meš}-ša) “her sons” (nominative plural + suffix); mārīša (DUMU-ša) “her son” (genitive + suffix): ana mārīša “to her son”
glossary.nadûm: to cast, throw (a charge; a body into the river): iddi, nadû, iddû · also to leave lying (a field): ittadi “he has left (it) lying” · of a flock: ṣēnī ana eqlim iddi “he turned the sheep loose into a field” · inaddûši (i-na-[ad]-du-u-ši) “they shall throw her” (present, plural, with -ši): ana mê inaddûši “they shall throw her into the water”
glossary.nadānum: to give, pay: inaddin, iddinam, iddinušum; nadānim “to give” · iddin “he gave”; ana kaspim nadānum “to sell”: inaddinūma (present, plural) “they shall sell, and …” · iddin, iddinu “he gave” (preterite; the subjunctive -u in a ša- or inūma clause); iddinma “he gave, and”; …in, …din in broken forms; inaddin “he shall give”: ana damqaršu inaddin “he shall give to his merchant” · ittadinma (it-ta-di-in-ma) “he has given, and” (perfect); inaddinu (i-na-ad-di-nu) “(which) he gives” (present, with the subjunctive -u) · ittandin (it-ta-an-di-in, perfect with an extra -n-) “he has handed over”: ana kiššātim ittandin “he handed over into service”; ittadin (it-ta-din) “he has given”, i.e. sold; ana maṣṣarūtim inaddin “he gives for safekeeping”; iddinūšumma “they gave him, and” · inaddin also of a woman, “she shall give” · inaddišši (i-na-ad-di-iš-ši) “he/she shall give her” (the n of the stem swallowed before -ši), of a sale: ana kaspim inaddišši “she may sell her”, ul inaddišši “she shall not sell her”
glossary.nadānum-N: N-stem of nadānum: to be given: innaddin “it shall be given”, innaddiššumma “it shall be given to him” · innadnušum (preterite, subjunctive -u, dative -šum) “(which) was given to him”
glossary.našûm: to bear, carry: ittanašši “he shall bear (the penalty)” · našû (na-šu-u, stative with the subjunctive -u) “(that) he carried”: mimma ša našû “anything that he carried” · ittanaššiši (it-ta-na-aš-ši-ši, Gtn present + -ši) “he shall keep carrying (supporting) her”
glossary.naṣārum: to guard, keep watch over, protect: inaṣṣarma (present, with -ma) “he shall guard, and …”
glossary.parāsum-N: N-stem (passive) of parāsum “to decide”: ipparrasma (ip-pa-ar-ra-aš-ma, present with -ma) “it shall be decided, and”; the present without -ma is ipparras “it shall be decided”
glossary.pānum: front, face: ina pani “in front of” · panīša ištakan “she has set her face”: the idiom for making up one’s mind, resolving to do something; with ana + infinitive “to …” (panīšu, panīša “his, her face”)
glossary.qabûm: to speak, say: iqbû, iqtabi, iqabbûma
glossary.rakāsum-D: D-stem of rakāsum “to bind”: to bind (by agreement), contract with (Harper: “to contract with”): urtakkis (ur-ta-ak-ki-is, perfect, with the t of the perfect after the first sign); who the subject is rests on the context
glossary.rašûm-Š: to cause to acquire (Š-stem of rašûm “to acquire, get”; double accusative): ušaršušu (u-šar-šu-šu) “who has made him acquire (children)” (ušarši + the subjunctive -u + -šu “him”); the analysis of the ending is UNCERTAIN
glossary.râmum: to love: irammu (i-ra-am-mu, present), with the subjunctive -u after ša: ša irammu “whom he/she loves”
glossary.sapāḫum-D: D-stem of sapāḫum “to scatter”: to scatter, neglect (Harper: “to scatter, to neglect”), said of a house or household: uzappaḫ (u-za-ap-pa-aḫ, present, 3rd person)
glossary.tamkārum: merchant (written tam-KAR §32, DAM.GÀR §40): the ransom-fronting, land-buying businessman of the code · written dam-qar, dam-qar-um (the common syllabic spelling of the merchant): damqar, damqarum “the merchant” (nominative), damqaršu “his merchant” · written DAM.GÀR as a Sumerogram (Harper tamkaru [DAM-GAR]; two signs on the plate): tamkārum, tamkāram, tamkārim, tamkāršu
glossary.ummum: mother: ana ummišu “to his mother”, ummašu urabbāšu “his mother shall raise him”
glossary.uzubbûm: UNCERTAIN: divorce payment, severance (uzubbûm): ana uzubbîm “as a divorce payment” (u-zu-ub-bi-im, genitive after ana); the reading is Harper’s and the word is rare
glossary.wabālum: to bring, carry: itbalam “he brought”, lū ublam “let me bring” · ublū (preterite, plural, in a ša-clause) “(the water) carried off”
glossary.walādum: to bear, give birth to: ūlidušum (ul-du-šum) “(whom) she bore to him” (preterite ūlid, the long ū of a w-initial verb, with the subjunctive -u and the dative -šum; Harper’s spelling is shortened, so the vowels of the form are UNCERTAIN) · ittalad (it-ta-la-ad, perfect) “she has borne” · ūlid (u-li-id, preterite) “she bore”, ūldu (ul-du, with subjunctive -u)
glossary.warkatum: the circumstances, the facts of the case: warkassu “his case” (warkat + šu, t+š → ss) · UNCERTAIN: warkassa (wa-ar-ka-za) “her case” (what is examined and decided) and “her estate” (what she leaves behind), the second reading resting on the context
glossary.warki: after, behind: warkišu “after him, in his absence”
glossary.wašābum: to sit: ul uššab “he shall not sit” (the stone writes uš-ta-ab — a carver’s slip Harper flags) · to dwell: wāšbum (participle, contracted) “the dweller, the tenant” (a conjectured reading, aš-bu-u[m]); wa… “dwell-” in broken forms · stative wašbat (wa-aš-ba-at) “she dwells, lives”: ša ina gagîm lā wašbat “who does not live in the cloister” · stative wašib (wa-ši-ib-ma, with -ma) “he is staying”: ina ḫarrānim wašib “he is staying on the road” · present uššab “she shall live” (uš-ša-ab) and uššamma (uš-ša-am-ma, the b becoming m before -ma) · infinitive wašābam (wa-ša-ba-am) “to live”, in the accusative after a verb
glossary.waṣûm: to go out; ūṣiamma “he came forward” · wuṣîm (wa-ṣi-im, the infinitive wuṣûm in the genitive after ana) “to go out” · waṣīma (wa-ṣi-ma, with -ma) and waṣiat (wa-ṣi-a-at, stative 3rd feminine) “going out”; the PI sign reads wa or wu, ZI is read ṣi, and the nuance of the form is UNCERTAIN
glossary.zakālum: UNCERTAIN: to play the fool (Harper): izakkil (i-za-ak-ki-il, present, 3rd person), used with the noun zikiltum of the same root; the sense rests on Harper’s glossary, which files the verb as šakālu “to play the part of a fool”
glossary.zikiltum: UNCERTAIN: folly, the part of a fool (Harper “the part of a fool”; his glossary files it as šikiltu, though his text spells zi-): zikiltam (zi-ki-il-tam, accusative), set beside the verb zakālum of the same root; the pair is Harper’s sense and UNCERTAIN by later standards
glossary.zinništum: woman (written with the single sign SAL, ŠAL in Harper): zinništam, zinništim, zinništum
glossary.zêrum: to hate, loathe: izīrūma “he hated, and” (preterite izīr + the subjunctive -u after aššum + -ma, in “he hated his city and fled”); the reading rests on the context
glossary.šakānum: to set, place: išakkanūšumma “they shall set for him (a term), and” · išakkanūšum (present, plural, dative -šum) “they shall place (it) for him”, i.e. count it to him · iššakkan (iš-ša-ak-ka-an, N-stem present) “it shall be put”: ul iššakkan “it shall not be put (in the account)” · to set, put, impose: ištakan (iš-ta-ka-an, perfect, “has set”), išakkan (present) — išakkanšima (i-ša-ak-ka-an-ši-ma, with -ši and -ma) “he/she shall set (it) on her, and”, as in abbuttam išakkan
glossary.šalāmum-D: D-stem of šalāmum “to be whole, sound”: to make good, restore (Harper: “to restore”): ušallamma (u-ša-lam-ma) “he shall make good, and”
glossary.šanûm: another, a second one: ana šanîm “to another”, šanûm “another man” · feminine šanītum “another (woman)”: šanītam, šanītim (ša-ni-tam, ša-ni-tim), in the accusative and genitive
glossary.šarākum: to give away, hand over: ištarak
glossary.šeriqtum: dowry, what the bride brings from her father’s house (§138 ša ištu bīt abiša ublam “which she brought from her father’s house”): šeriqtam “the dowry”, šeriqtaša “her dowry”. Harper reads it with q (še-ri-iq-ta-ša, the sign IG read iq) and later editions with k; UNCERTAIN in the form, the meaning rests on §138
glossary.šugītum: UNCERTAIN: a class of woman named in §137, written {šal}šu-gi₄-tim (Harper prints šu-ge-tim): šugītim “(to) a šugītum”; the law sets her beside an ordinary wife as a woman who may bear children; her exact status is not known
glossary.šumma: if — the word that opens every law of the code
glossary.šuāti: that, the aforesaid · as the independent pronoun “him”: šuāti u bīšašu “him and his goods”
glossary.šī: she, that (feminine pronoun, as the independent word): ŠAL.GEŠ.TIN.NA šī “that tavern-keeper”; the masculine is šū
glossary.ḫarrānum: road; campaign: ḫarrān šarrim “the king’s campaign” (spelled ḫar-ra-an, or carved with the road-sign KASKAL) · journey, the merchant’s trading trip: ana ḫarrānim “on a journey” (the editors print ḫarranim; the spelling ḫar-ra-nim is uncertain here), ina ḫarrānim “on the journey” · UNCERTAIN: Harper “way, road, journey, errand”: ḫarrānša (ḫa-ra-an-ša) “her journey”, a payment she does not get — a guess at a travel-allowance (Harper’s own translation: “on her departure”)
glossary.ḫiṭītum: UNCERTAIN: sin, fault, defect: ḫiṭītam (ḫi-ṭi-tam, accusative); Harper prints ḫi-di-tam, but the middle sign DI also reads ṭi, and his glossary does not list the word, so the identification rests on the sign reading and the context
glossary.ḫubullum: debt, an interest-bearing loan: ḫubullum; bēl ḫubullim “the creditor” · ḫubullam, ḫubullim, written ḫu-bu-ul-lam / ḫu-bu-ul-li-im, and also ḪAR.RA (perhaps the same word, taken so from context, UNCERTAIN): ana ḫubullim “as a loan”, ša ḫubullam ilqû “who took a loan”
glossary.ṣabātum: to seize: iṣṣabat, ṣabtu · stative with the subjunctive -u: adi kirâm ṣabtu “as long as he holds the orchard” (with Harper’s kirûm: “as long as the orchard is held”) · iṣṣabtamma (iṣ-ṣa-ab-tam-ma) “she seized (them), and” (perfect with the ventive -am and -ma): lā iṣṣabtamma “and she did not seize” · iṣbassuma (iṣ-ba-zu-ma, ZU for -ssu) “it seized him, and” (preterite iṣbat + -šu + -ma), of a debt seizing a man · iṣṣabtūšu (iṣ-ṣa-ab-tu-šu) “they seized him” (perfect, plural, with -šu “him”); iṣṣabat (iṣ-ṣa-ba-at) “he has seized (his wife)” (perfect) · iṣṣabassi (iṣ-ṣa-ba-az-zi) “it has seized her” (perfect + -ši, t + š said ss); present plural iṣabbatū (i-ṣa-ba-tu) “they shall seize”; preterite with the subjunctive iṣbatu; infinitive with suffix ṣabātiša “seizing her”
glossary.ṭuppum: the clay tablet; the deed: ṭuppašu iḫḫeppi “his tablet shall be smashed” — the sale annulled physically
